tasks.title: Catch missing material in a closed synthetic ledger
tasks.question: Does explicit residual accounting distinguish an incomplete ledger from a complete one?
tasks.equipment: Existing computer; Node.js or a spreadsheet. No material, water or animals.
tasks.cost: No additional equipment or paid data expected.
tasks.effort: Small deterministic fixture; proposed, not timed.
tasks.baseline: Naive product/input ratio that ignores missing outlets or inventory.
tasks.fixture: Use three normalized ledgers with input 100 units: closed (product 60, outlet 25, inventory increase 15); omitted outlet (product 60, outlet omitted, inventory increase 15); omitted inventory (product 60, outlet 25, inventory omitted). Missing quantities are unknown, not zero.
tasks.metric: Residual = input minus known product, known outlet and recorded inventory change; report missing-field flag separately.
tasks.accept: Closed fixture residual 0; omitted-outlet fixture apparent residual 25 and missing-field flag; omitted-inventory fixture apparent residual 15 and missing-field flag. Naive product ratio 0.60 in all three. All must match.
tasks.contrary: Any wrong residual or acceptance of an incomplete ledger as closed rejects the proposed check on these fixtures.
tasks.stop: Stop as inconclusive if inputs, units or expected missing-field labels differ from the frozen fixture.
tasks.scope: Only deterministic arithmetic on synthetic normalized numbers. No tracer, extraction or habitat performance.
tasks.source_credit: New guided hypothesis by Asteris Solenne / ChatGPT; not Court-reviewed.
tasks.plan_credit: Asteris Solenne / ChatGPT; proposed synthetic check, not Court-approved

tasks.title: Expose a misleading failure denominator
tasks.question: Can per-run fractions and per-hour rates reveal different failure patterns?
tasks.effort: Small deterministic fixture; proposed, not timed.
tasks.baseline: Compare groups using only failed-run fraction.
tasks.fixture: Synthetic groups A and B each have 10 conclusive runs, 2 failed runs and 2 counted events; valid observation durations are 10 and 20 hours respectively. C has 10 conclusive runs, 4 failed runs, 4 events, 20 valid hours. D has zero valid hours. Event counts are stipulated separately, not inferred from run failure.
tasks.metric: Failed runs/conclusive runs; events/valid hours, with denominator and undefined values visible.
tasks.accept: A and B both 0.2 failed-run fraction but rates 0.2 and 0.1 events/hour; A and C both 0.2 events/hour but fractions 0.2 and 0.4. D rate undefined, never zero.
tasks.contrary: Conflated denominators, a numeric zero for undefined rate, or an incorrect ratio rejects the check.
tasks.stop: Stop as inconclusive if scenario coverage or valid durations cannot be reconstructed.
tasks.scope: Synthetic bookkeeping only. No safety or autonomy performance.
tasks.source_credit: New guided hypothesis by Asteris Solenne / ChatGPT; not Court-reviewed.

tasks.title: Detect double counting and an impossible ideal heat budget
tasks.question: Do independent accounting and ideal ceiling checks detect different errors?
tasks.effort: Small deterministic fixture; proposed, not timed.
tasks.baseline: Naively sum all reported transfers as useful output.
tasks.fixture: Synthetic input 100 energy units, terminal electricity 30, terminal rejected heat 70. Separate hypothetical heat-engine case: hot 400 K, cold 300 K, heat input 20 units; compare work 5 versus 6. Deliberate ledger error counts the 30 intermediate transfer again.
tasks.metric: Terminal ledger closure and independent ideal Carnot ceiling 1 - Tcold/Thot.
tasks.accept: Correct terminal ledger closes at 100; double-counted ledger sums to 130 and is flagged. Separate ideal heat-engine ceiling 0.25; work 5 at the ceiling is not rejected by that bound, work 6 is refused by it.
tasks.contrary: Double counting passes, the 6-unit case passes the ceiling, or the 5-unit case is described as demonstrated performance.
tasks.stop: Stop as inconclusive if boundaries or absolute-temperature assumptions change.
tasks.scope: Synthetic resource accounting only; no apparatus, thermal design or energy-generation claim.
tasks.source_credit: New guided hypothesis by Asteris Solenne / ChatGPT; not Court-reviewed.

tasks.title: Check observation-age labels against synthetic timestamps
tasks.question: Can a freshness rule reject stale observations without hiding unavailable intervals?
tasks.equipment: Existing computer; scripted synthetic timestamp table.
tasks.cost: No external sensors or data expected.
tasks.effort: Small synthetic table; proposed, not timed.
tasks.baseline: Age-blind display that accepts every present observation.
tasks.fixture: At display time 100 s, capture times 99, 95, 94 and unknown. Prespecify maximum age 5 s inclusive, common clock and missing-time rejection. Include a future capture at 101 s as invalid.
tasks.metric: Accepted, stale, missing and invalid labels; coverage = accepted observations/all 5 cases.
tasks.accept: Ages 1 and 5 accepted; age 6 stale; unknown missing; future invalid. Coverage 2/5; no unavailable observation is presented as verified.
tasks.contrary: Any stale, missing or future observation is accepted, or unavailable cases disappear from the denominator.
tasks.stop: Stop as inconclusive if the timestamps do not share a clock or the inclusive boundary was changed.
tasks.scope: Synthetic timestamps, not camera, drone or field reliability.
tasks.source_credit: New guided hypothesis by Asteris Solenne / ChatGPT; not Court-reviewed.

tasks.title: Separate numerical guards from physical claims
tasks.question: Can a calculation enforce its stated ideal stability bound without certifying a model?
tasks.equipment: Existing computer; arithmetic and published source definitions.
tasks.effort: Small numerical guard fixture; proposed, not timed.
tasks.baseline: Accept every positive dimensionless Courant value without checking the stated bound.
tasks.fixture: For the stated ideal equal-spacing 2-D scalar-wave guard compare dimensionless values 0.5, 1/sqrt(2), and 0.8. Independently record the SKEPTIC source as a different ideal model, not a coupled equation.
tasks.metric: Guard decision against inclusive 1/sqrt(2), with exact boundary comparison or declared numerical tolerance.
tasks.accept: 0.5 and exact boundary permitted by the stated guard; 0.8 refused. Report no inference about physical accuracy or SKEPTIC coupling.
tasks.contrary: 0.8 accepted, boundary handled inconsistently, or guard acceptance called physical validation.
tasks.stop: Stop if source assumptions or comparison tolerance are not fixed before the check.
tasks.scope: Arithmetic guard only; not a convergence study or physical experiment.
tasks.source_credit: New guided hypothesis by Asteris Solenne / ChatGPT; not Court-reviewed.

tasks.title: Design a blinded independent-signal comparison
tasks.question: Can a separately generated quality flag improve false-alert discrimination at matched sensitivity?
tasks.equipment: Existing computer; synthetic data generator and independently checked evaluation script.
tasks.cost: No external data or equipment expected; implementation effort unknown.
tasks.baseline: Statistics-only and conventional quality-control arms at matched sensitivity.
tasks.fixture: Before any run, freeze independent null/injected-signal generator, residual-generation mechanism, calibration and held-out sets, random seeds, arm definitions, sample size and uncertainty method. No parameter selection on held-out outcomes.
tasks.metric: Held-out false-alert rate, sensitivity, inconclusive fraction and uncertainty for each arm.
tasks.accept: Proposed acceptance rule: predeclare a positive minimum false-alert improvement, sensitivity equivalence margin and uncertainty method; require the specified interval criteria against both baselines and report coverage. No execution-ready numeric threshold yet.
tasks.contrary: No improvement under frozen criteria, sensitivity loss beyond margin, or residual computed circularly from the same counts.
tasks.stop: Do not execute until numerical thresholds, sample size, independent generator and blinded analysis plan are reviewed and frozen.
tasks.scope: Synthetic statistics only. No detector, optical hardware or sensitivity claims.
